The last 3 years I've been doing 2.5 miles a day ~5 days a week. Over the past two months I've been doing a lot of 10 and 20 milers. My knees are forcing me to stop though. I can't even do an old 2.5 miler without them alerting me.

My question is will my knees always hurt? I weigh 160 lbs now (kinda fat) but if I cut it down ten or twenty pounds maybe that would be kneesier? I have been icing and bracing my knees daily but it seems like a losing battle.

Hard to say since everyone is different. There's an 80+ year-old runner in my neighborhood who still gets out there 3 times a week to run. He's slower than his wife now but he can still clock a decent 5k time and can still do up to 10 miles or so. There's another runner here that's in his 60s that hasn't run in decades because of his knees and hips. He can ride a bike like a madman but struggles to walk without limping. Me, I'm in my 40s and (knock on wood) don't have any knee pain. I'm 6 foot and 240 pounds.

I would say if your knees hurt, try slowing down, going shorter distances, and checking your shoes. When my legs start to get odd pains (knees, hips, ankles, etc.), it's usually because my shoes need to be replaced. It could also be those longer runs that have come too fast in your training. Maybe cut the long runs to see if that helps.

I know losing weight would help, but I'm a big guy myself so I know that's easier said than done. I wouldn't worry about that unless there's been a sudden change (up or down) with your weight. Maybe take a few weeks off or alternate biking or something to let your legs recover then start over again to see if the pain comes back.

I ran for years with a torn meniscus and only found out when my knee painfully locked in the gym. I just ran through the discomfort for years. I suggest you do not do this. Go visit a sports medicine knee specialist, and if you have the time and money, see a sports phys therapist. Mine got me back running two weeks after surgery and my knees feel like new.
